results.label: this tree ships the plan gate (src/bots/plan-gate.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the vocabulary is a closed list of named facts, each with a documented line
every documented line parses as a MACHINE rule — the documentation cannot drift from the engine
and each fact appears exactly once
the compare facts document their own operator, so a trader never has to guess the direction
a fact with a closed value set publishes that set, so a client can render the choices
a line that does not start with `require` is prose — context for the human, never a rule for the engine
a `require` line naming a fact the vocabulary does not know is reported as unrecognised, NOT passed as satisfied
an empty line is prose rather than an empty rule
a floor cannot be written as a ceiling: `require min_rr <= 2` is unrecognised, not a rule
and a ceiling cannot be written as a floor: `require risk >= 1` is unrecognised
a boolean fact takes no operator or value
an enum fact must be one of its own values (a misspelling is not a silent pass)
a compare fact must have a positive number
`min_rr >= 2` is met at the boundary (2.0R) and refused just below it
`risk <= 1` is met at the boundary (1%) and refused above it
the grade ladder is ordered A+ > A > B > C > D, so `>= B` is met by A+ and refused by C
a stood-down setup cannot satisfy a plan that asked for a tradeable grade
an enum comparison is case-insensitive on both sides
a boolean fact is refused only when it is known false
a fact the caller did not hand over is UNKNOWN — never `met`
and every read that could not be made is unknown: undefined, null and NaN alike
every documented line is a machine rule, so the sweep below covers the whole vocabulary
with nothing readable, every rule is unknown and NOT ONE veto is fabricated
and an unknown rule carries no sentence either (a refusal must always be a measured false)
a refusal names the trader’s own plan, its version and its own rule text
it states the fact that failed, and quotes the episode’s own non-negotiable
and it is exactly one sentence per refused rule, in the plan’s own order
a path with no trader is `not_consulted`, which is a different token from a plan that failed to read
no plan is `no_plan` and blocks nothing, with the reason in the note
two active plans are reported as ambiguous WITH both names, never silently intersected or picked
an unreadable plan is `unavailable` and carries the reason, so a broken read can never look like compliance
a ready plan reports what is enforced, what is prose and what is unrecognised — as three separate lists
the per-direction results ride the view, so a client can explain which side a rule refused
the limits name the vocabulary and deny every influence a gate could be mistaken for
nothing in the gate is money-shaped: no amount, P&L, equity or goal key anywhere in the payload
a plan whose rules were never written parses to zero rules, not to an error
a stored value that is not an array (or not JSON at all) also yields zero rules — the gate can never crash a signal
and it is reported as MALFORMED rather than as a plan with nothing to enforce
an array of strings is parsed in order, and blank entries are dropped rather than counted
and the counts a client renders are the parse’s own counts
the gate exposes no way to change a grade, a score, a cap or a price: the module exports no such setter
and it names that limit itself, so the refusal can never be quoted as a performance claim

scope: M56 pure: the plan gate’s vocabulary, parse and evaluation: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
